'''Tulpaa''' was an [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. It was located in the [[Rakatan Archipelago]], a group of worlds [[Colonist/Legends|settled]] by remnants of the collapsed [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. During the subsequent tens of [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]], the Rakatan [[Tulpaa tribe|tribes]] [[Makatak tribe|inhabiting]] Tulpaa and its fellow planet [[Makatak]] emerged as the most advanced of the Rakatan Archipelago worlds.

The Tulpaa and Makatak tribes both sent recovered Infinite Empire [[skipship]]s to search for exploitable resources and [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] on life-rich Unknown Regions planets. The emerging [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitivity]] of Tulpaa's [[Elders (Rakatan)|Elder]] [[Ruthic]] also facilitated the tribe's insight into other [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-powered technological artifacts of the Infinite Empire such as [[mind prison]]s. Additionally, Tulpaa attempted to complete the construction of a [[Star Forge (Tulpaa)|Star Forge]] [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] [[Factory/Legends|factory]], an effort in which the planet competed with Makatak.

==Description==
A terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]], Tulpaa<ref name="TUR" /> was located in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] [[Star system/Legends|star system]] of the [[Tulpaa system/Legends|same name]].<ref name="EAOC" /> It was a part of the [[Rakatan Archipelago]], a fragmented group of unaligned planets that stretched across the entirety of the Unknown Regions.<ref name="TUR" />

==History==
===An advanced remnant===
[[File:Rakata-TUR.jpg|thumb|left|260px|Tulpaa was inhabited by a tribe of the Rakata species.]]
Tulpaa was [[Colonist/Legends|settled]] by [[Tulpaa tribe|one]] of the tribes of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[Species/Legends|species]] fleeing the collapse of the Rakatan [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]]<ref name="TUR" /> around [[25,200 BBY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Due to the [[Rakatan plague|plague]] that led to the empire's downfall, the surviving Rakata lost their natural [[Force-sensitive/Legends|sensitivity]] to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], thereby rendering much of their advanced Force-powered technology inoperable. As a result, the worlds of the Rakatan Archipelago regressed to a primitive state.<ref name="TUR" />

During the subsequent tens of [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]], Tulpaa and the planet [[Makatak]] both became home to the most technologically advanced Rakata in the Unknown Regions. The [[Priest/Legends|priests]], also known as the [[Elders (Rakatan)|Elders]], of both the Tulpaa and [[Makatak tribe]]s eventually exhumed buried Rakatan [[Starship/Legends|starships]] known as [[skipship]]s, thereby regaining interstellar spaceflight ability.<ref name="TUR" />

The [[Force-drive|hyperspace drives]] of the skipships operated by zeroing in on planets with rich biospheres that had high concentrations of the Force, and the Force-dependent nature of the technology meant that the Rakatan tribes were unable to control the process. Another effect of the skipships' operating principles was that Tulpaa and Makatak came to compete over the same life-rich worlds, from which the Rakata harvested [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] and natural resources such as metals and [[Ore/Legends|ores]], compressed [[Gas/Legends|gasses]], and [[Radiation/Legends|radioactive]] [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]].<ref name="TUR" />

===Mind prisons===
[[File:Mindprisonblue.png|thumb|right|200px|The Tulpaa tribe possessed dozens of mind prisons.]]
The Rakatan Elders on Makatak and Tulpaa tinkered with other crumbling inventions of the Infinite Empire, as well. Both tribes possessed dozens of [[mind prison]]s, ancient boxes that each contained an infinite expanse of [[Color/Legends|white]] nothingness and that were used as [[Prison/Legends|prison]] devices. The Rakata on Tulpaa and Makatak attempted to puzzle out a way to unlock the mind prisons; however, since such a feat could only be performed via use of the Force, the technology remained beyond their reach.<ref name="TUR" />

At some point, Elder [[Ruthic]]&mdash;who, uniquely among the Rakata, over the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] had been gradually developing a connection to the Force&mdash;[[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exiled]] her rivals among the Tulpaa tribe's leadership into a [[Tulpaa mind prison|mind prison]] and herself became the head of the tribe. Ruthic's growing Force-sensitivity gave her tribe a significant advantage due to the insight she gained into the Infinite Empire's technology. As a result, skipships were dispatched from Tulpaa by the hundreds to scour the Unknown Regions for slaves and resources.<ref name="TUR" />

===A new Star Forge===
In addition, Tulpaa and Makatak were competing to complete the construction on half-[[Kilometer/Legends|kilometer]]-large scaled-down versions of the [[Star Forge]],<ref name="TUR" /> an [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] [[Factory/Legends|factory]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> that was powered by the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]<ref name="CSWE Rakata">{{CSWECite|III|76|Rakata}}</ref> and was capable of nearly-infinite output<ref name="TEA" /> of [[Warship/Legends|warships]] and [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]].<ref name="CSWE Star Forge">{{CSWECite|III|187|Star Forge}}</ref> By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of Ruthic's leadership, the metal skeleton of the new [[Star Forge (Tulpaa)|Star Forge]] was taking shape in the [[Atmosphere/Legends|skies]] of Tulpaa. [[Raspir]], a [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] [[Magic/Legends|magician]] who was released from the same mind prison Ruthic exiled her opponents to and subsequently resided in the Force-sensitive Elder's [[Ruthic's ruling temple|ruling temple]], provided Ruthic with wise advice that allowed her to bend the manufacturing facilities of the Tulpaa Star Forge to her will.<ref name="TUR" />

{{RPGseed}}
At some point, a group of individuals targeted for [[Saboteur/Legends|sabotage]] the Star Forge under construction over Tulpaa. In another instance, a Force-sensitive individual helped the Rakata of one of the Makatak and Tulpaa tribes to open a mind prison. The device then released long-[[Prisoner/Legends|imprisoned]], unhinged [[Death/Legends|killers]], such as criminals of the [[Sharu/Legends|Sharu]] species and [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]] [[Soldier/Legends|super-soldiers]].<ref name="TUR" />
{{Endgame}}

==Inhabitants==
{{Main|Tulpaa tribe}}
Tulpaa was inhabited by a tribe of the Rakata, a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] species that spoke the [[Rakata (language)|Rakata]] [[Language/Legends|language]]. The tribe was among the more enlightened Rakatan societies that survived the collapse of the Infinite Empire, especially when compared with the more primitive and barbarous Rakatan worlds of [[Fitomp]] and [[Hilak]]. In comparison to those planets, Tulpaa saw less [[Standard day/Legends|day]]-to-day [[Blood/Legends|bloodshed]], but the innate, violent conqueror nature of the Rakata, coupled with the species' longing for its lost Force-sensitivity, maintained the powerful desire of the Tulpaa tribe to restore the former glory of the Infinite Empire.<ref name="TUR" />

In addition to the Rakata, Tulpaa was home to members of the [[Gengh-Noghri]], an [[Subspecies/Legends|offshoot]] of the [[Noghri/Legends|Noghri]] species<ref name="TUR" /> that was native to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] planet [[Honoghr/Legends|Honoghr]].<ref name="TEA" /> The Gengh-Noghri were brought to Tulpaa from the slave stock the Infinite Empire had drawn from Honoghr, and two members of the subspecies served as [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] of Tulpaa's Elder Ruthic.<ref name="TUR" />

==Behind the scenes==
Tulpaa was introduced in ''[[The Unknown Regions]]'', a sourcebook for the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' that was developed by [[Wizards of the Coast]]. ''The Unknown Regions'' was written by [[Sterling Hershey]], [[Rodney Thompson]], and [[Daniel Wallace]], and was published in [[2010]]. The book includes several adventure seeds for use with the ''Star Wars Roleplaying Game''. This article assumes full completion of those scenarios.<ref name="TUR" />
